## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a cross-platform RN native module that performs real-time on-device ML inference, bridging frames from the camera to a GPU-accelerated model, with careful backpressure, lifecycle, and privacy considerations.

## Key Concepts
- RN native modules: TurboModules/JSI bridging for cross-platform APIs
- On-device ML: GPU acceleration (Metal on iOS, Vulkan/NNAPI on Android)
- Concurrency: dedicated frame producer thread, GPU worker, bounded frame/detection queues
- Backpressure: drop or throttle frames to avoid JS backlog while keeping UI responsive
- Lifecycle: clean shutdown, model swap without leaks, pause/resume semantics

## Code Example
```javascript
// Implementation sketch (pseudo)
RNDetector.startDetection(modelPath, {fps:15})
RNDetector.onDetections((detections) => handleDetections(detections))
RNDetector.switchModel(newModelPath)
RNDetector.pause()
RNDetector.resume()
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you measure and bound memory usage across devices with different GPUs?
- How would you secure data privacy if the model occasionally uses cloud fallback?

## Performance Optimization Strategies

### Code Splitting & Lazy Loading
- Use React.lazy() for screen components wrapped in Suspense
- Implement route-based code splitting to reduce initial bundle size
- Leverage Metro bundler's RAM bundles for improved memory efficiency

### Memory Management
- Proper cleanup in useEffect hooks to prevent memory leaks
- Avoid closures in long-lived components that retain references
- Use WeakMap/WeakSet for large data structures
- Implement proper event listener cleanup

### List Optimization
```javascript
<FlatList
  data={items}
  getItemLayout={(data, index) => ({length: ITEM_HEIGHT, offset: ITEM_HEIGHT * index, index})}
  removeClippedSubviews={true}
  maxToRenderPerBatch={10}
  windowSize={10}
  initialNumToRender={10}
/>
```

### Engine & Build Optimizations
- Use Hermes JavaScript engine for better performance
- Implement bundle splitting and code optimization
- Utilize React.memo() and useMemo() for expensive computations
- Profile and optimize re-renders with React DevTools
